title: What Mexico Can (And Cannot) Control   - Americas Quarterly
gist: This record is the issue page for Vanessa Rubio-Marquez's lead editorial on Mexico, containing a standfirst and the issue's table of contents rather than the essay body. It lists companion pieces on China's trade shock, Latin American tech and data centers, Nicaragua, illicit cigarettes, the ELN and AmericasBarometer data.

insights.claim: AQ's lead editorial argues Mexico can focus on navigating tensions with the US while putting its own house in better order, according to the standfirst by a former policymaker.
insights.speaker: VANESSA RUBIO-MÁRQUEZ
insights.so_what: Signals the issue's framing; the full argument is covered in the cover-story summary pieces.

insights.claim: The issue pairs the Mexico editorial with Susan Segal's argument that US-Mexico-Canada integration is a success story worth celebrating.
insights.speaker: VANESSA RUBIO-MÁRQUEZ
insights.locator: The Immense Value of North America

insights.claim: Marcos Troyjo's piece 'From China Shock to China Choke' says China is reshaping the global landscape with its trade preferences, with a great deal at stake for Latin America and the world.
insights.speaker: VANESSA RUBIO-MÁRQUEZ
insights.so_what: Only a one-line teaser is available; no argument detail in this record.
insights.locator: From China Shock to China Choke

insights.claim: Other issue pieces cover Latin America's high-tech value chain, a data center powerhouse debate, Nicaraguan exile journalism, China's raised stakes in the region, illicit cigarettes, the ELN guerrillas and a Noam Lupu Q&A on AmericasBarometer 2026 democracy data.
insights.speaker: VANESSA RUBIO-MÁRQUEZ
